clue.text: A doctor employed outside hospital got waylaid

parts.note: MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

indicators.note: the word for employed is placed around the hospital abbreviation

parts.note: something employed has been used

explanation.surface: Someone with a doctor working outside a hospital was set upon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employed' is a synonym for the outer piece, not a clue about the doctor's job; 'got' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To waylay someone is to lie in wait and attack them by surprise.

clue.text: She always has stew

parts.note: aye is an old or poetic word for always

indicators.note: to stew is to cook in a jumble, so the letters of has are mixed up

explanation.surface: A woman who is forever making casseroles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' rearranges HAS into SHA. In H. Rider Haggard's novel She, the immortal queen 'She-who-must-be-obeyed' is named Ayesha.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Haggard's adventure novel She bears this name.

clue.text: Support children in care retrogressively

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
wards are children placed under the protection of a guardian or court

explanation.surface: Funding for looked-after children is going the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving retrogressively means going in the reverse direction, toward the rear.

clue.text: Refused food whilst designing adverts

indicators.note: designing something is arranging it anew, so these letters are laid out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: An advertising creative was too busy working on campaigns to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whilst' is a link word; the fodder is ADVERTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A person deprived of food, or who declines it, goes hungry.

clue.text: The Spanish piano piece upset English composer

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word for the piano piece upside down, reading it bottom to top

parts.note: a rag is a ragtime piece, typically played on piano

explanation.surface: A Spanish piano tune annoyed a composer from England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns RAG into GAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Elgar, of the Enigma Variations, is one of England's best-known composers.

clue.text: Rum? It's awfully commonplace

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters of Rum and It's are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a strange thing is dreadfully ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: A truism is a statement so obvious it is banal, a platitude.

clue.text: Cleric from Ireland? Quite the contrary!

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a title for a clergyman
Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland, so it describes something Irish

explanation.surface: Asked whether a priest comes from Ireland, someone answers that the opposite is true.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying the opposite is the case is to state the converse or contrary of what was claimed.

clue.text: Bringing back a swan in it is absurd

indicators.note: the reversed bird is placed inside the word it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: bringing back means the word for the swan is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: Someone thinks reintroducing a swan into a scheme is silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bringing back' turns PEN into NEP, which goes 'in' IT. 'a' and 'is' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means foolish or clumsily unsuitable, as an absurd remark would be.

clue.text: Harm head of the security services

indicators.note: head of X puts the chief after the security services' possessive, so of orders the pieces

parts.note: MI, Military Intelligence (as in MI5 and MI6), with the possessive 's
a chief is a head or leader

explanation.surface: Damage done by the boss of British intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of the security services' is read as MI's chief; 'of' is a link word showing whose chief it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischief can mean damage or injury caused to someone, as in 'do yourself a mischief'.

clue.text: Husband demands jam

definitions.meaning: to husband resources is to use them sparingly and save them

explanation.surface: A married man insists on fruit preserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husband' is a verb here, not a married man; 'demands' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To save resources carefully is to preserve them; a fruit preserve is a sweet spread.

clue.text: Discussion in the photographers' swap shop

definitions.meaning: a debate where opinions are traded
a cryptic sense: a place where camera users trade their pictures of scenes

explanation.surface: A conversation takes place at a market where photographers trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; the second reading treats views as photos of landscapes being traded.
explanation.definitionFit: A discussion is a trading of opinions; a photographers' swap would trade scenic pictures.

clue.text: Yet we remain in a state of suspense

indicators.note: we remain in tells us the pronoun stays inside the other word

parts.note: Chambers gives hover as a noun meaning a state of suspense or uncertainty

explanation.surface: Someone says, nonetheless, that we are still waiting anxiously.
explanation.definitionFit: Yet and the answer are both conjunctions meaning nevertheless or but.

clue.text: Extend a prison sentence

definitions.meaning: slang for a term in jail

explanation.definitionFit: To lengthen is to pull out; prison slang calls a term inside the same word.

clue.text: Made director act as Shylock

indicators.note: made means formed or created, so the letters of director are formed into a new word

explanation.surface: A film director was cast in the role of the moneylender in The Merchant of Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'act as' is a link word. Shylock is Shakespeare's moneylender, and the name is used generally for a hard-hearted lender.
explanation.definitionFit: A lender is owed money by the borrower, as Shylock was owed by Antonio.

clue.text: They hold a girl up in Greece

indicators.note: the word They holds the reversed girl inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for the girl reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Some people are keeping a young woman waiting in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LASS into SSAL, which THEY 'hold'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thessaly is a region of central Greece.

clue.text: No longer one the French need to deport

parts.note: ex means former, no longer in that role
I is the Roman numeral for one
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A former partner, the French say, must be sent away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'need to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To banish is to send a person away from their country.

clue.text: Found society to promote research?

definitions.meaning: an organisation devoted to study, as in a research body

explanation.surface: Someone sets up a learned society for research.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up something is to establish it; a learned research body also bears the name.

clue.text: On trial for serving drinks?

definitions.meaning: the accused stands in the dock, facing the court
a cryptic sense: working behind the counter of a pub

explanation.surface: Someone facing charges is caught working in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; the question mark flags the playful pub sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner in court stands before the judge; a barman stands behind the pub counter.

clue.text: Italian poet offered Soviet news agency nothing

parts.note: TASS was the official news agency of the Soviet Union
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Moscow's news service gave a poet from Italy no coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offered' is a link word. Torquato Tasso wrote the epic Jerusalem Delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso was a sixteenth-century Renaissance writer from Sorrento.

clue.text: Direct old vicar back to the bishop's office

indicators.note: back means the word for the vicar is read in reverse

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a vicar's title
a see is a bishop's diocese or seat of authority

explanation.surface: Someone sends an elderly clergyman back to the bishop's headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns REV into VER; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To direct an operation is to supervise or manage it.

clue.text: Discharge duty without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the tax word surrounds the hesitation

parts.note: excise is a tax or duty on goods
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone carries out their obligations promptly and without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking, an old sense often used by setters.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise a power or function is to carry it out or discharge it.

clue.text: In a recent rally he emerged as chief

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the words a recent rally

explanation.surface: At a recent political rally a man emerged as leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'recent rally'; 'he emerged as' is link padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Central can mean principal or most important, as in the central issue.

clue.text: Cheers full-time sportsmen with sex appeal

parts.note: pros are professionals, full-time players
'it' is old slang for sex appeal, as in the 'It girl'

explanation.surface: A toast to attractive professional athletes.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosit is a German and Latin drinking toast, like saying 'your health'.

clue.text: Terrible hassle about parking. So unfortunate

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, round, the parking letter
terrible suggests something wrecked, so the letters of hassle are mixed up

parts.note: P is the sign for a car park or parking

explanation.surface: Finding a parking space was a dreadful bother; how unlucky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' shuffles HASSLE into HALESS, and 'about' puts it round P. 'So' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone luckless is unfortunate.

clue.text: Opt for stout

definitions.meaning: to ... for something is to choose it
stout here means fat, the adjective

explanation.definitionFit: To plump for is to choose decisively; plump also means chubby or fat.

clue.text: Row about a North German initially in Morocco

indicators.note: the word for row goes about, round, the other letters

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of North and German

explanation.surface: A northern German argues while visiting Morocco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel but is a line of seats. 'initially' gives NG, and TIER goes 'about' A plus NG.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangier is a port city in northern Morocco.

clue.text: Smack son in London gallery

indicators.note: the letter for son is put inside the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is an art gallery in London
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone hits their boy in an art museum in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smack' looks like a slap, but it is a noun meaning a flavour or hint.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack of something is a slight flavour or trace of it.

clue.text: EU expands vegetable production

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the European Union and used to stand for it
sprouts means grows or expands

explanation.surface: The European Union increases its output of vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: These small cabbage-like buds are a widely grown green vegetable crop.

clue.text: Rebuked for having knocked

definitions.meaning: struck a door or surface with sharp taps

explanation.surface: Someone was told off for banging on a door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rap means both to criticise sharply and to strike with quick blows.

clue.text: Quite determined the chap will have talent

parts.note: he'll is a contraction of he will
a bent is a natural talent or aptitude

explanation.surface: Someone is resolved that the man will be gifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set on doing something at any cost means being resolute.
